title: Indirect speech: statements, questions, and shifts
goal: Report statements, questions, and commands with natural subordinate word order, tense choices, and pronoun or time-place shifts.

objectives.statement: Report statements, questions, and commands with natural subordinate word order, tense choices, and pronoun or time-place shifts.

spans.value: Sara arrives at the office after a delayed bus. She has missed the morning meeting, and Jonas tells her what the others said.
Sara
Jeg rakk ikke møtet. Hva sa Liv?

blocks.translation: I didn’t make it to the meeting. What did Liv say?

spans.value: Jonas
Hun sa at toget til Bergen var innstilt, så hun jobbet hjemmefra.

blocks.translation: She said that the train to Bergen was cancelled, so she was working from home.

spans.value: Sara
Spurte hun om vi kunne flytte presentasjonen?

blocks.translation: Did she ask whether we could move the presentation?

spans.value: Jonas
Ja. Hun spurte om vi kunne ta den i morgen.

blocks.translation: Yes. She asked whether we could do it tomorrow.

spans.value: Jonas
Hun ba meg også om å sende kundene en melding i dag.

blocks.translation: She also asked me to send the clients a message today.

spans.value: Sara
Hva sa Amir?
Jonas
Han sa at han allerede hadde snakket med dem.

blocks.translation: He said that he had already spoken to them.

spans.value: Jonas
Han spurte også når Liv kom tilbake til kontoret.

blocks.translation: He also asked when Liv was coming back to the office.

spans.value: Sara
Hun skulle komme tilbake i dag, ikke sant?

blocks.translation: She was going to come back today, wasn’t she?

spans.value: Jonas
Ja. Da hun ringte i går, sa hun at hun skulle komme tilbake hit i dag.

blocks.translation: Yes. When she called yesterday, she said that she would come back here today.

spans.value: Sara
Kan du be henne om å ringe meg når hun er framme?

blocks.translation: Can you ask her to call me when she arrives?

spans.value: Jonas
Ja, jeg skal si at du vil at hun skal ringe deg.

blocks.translation: Yes, I’ll say that you want her to call you.

spans.value: Sara needs more than Liv’s exact words. She needs to know who said what, whether something was a statement, a question, or a request, and whether the message still applies now. Jonas therefore uses
indirect speech (indirekte tale)
: he reports the content of someone’s words without repeating the original conversation exactly.
Notice the three main patterns in the scene:

no.value: Hun sa at toget var innstilt.

en.value: She said that the train was cancelled.

no.value: Hun spurte om vi kunne flytte presentasjonen.

en.value: She asked whether we could move the presentation.

no.value: Hun ba meg om å sende kundene en melding.

en.value: She asked me to send the clients a message.

spans.value: The type of original message determines how the report begins, and the resulting subordinate clause structure determines word order. The reporting viewpoint guides tense, pronouns, and expressions such as i dag and her.
A reported statement normally uses a reporting verb followed by
at
, meaning that.

no.value: Liv sier at toget er innstilt.

en.value: Liv says that the train is cancelled.

no.value: Liv sa at toget var innstilt.

en.value: Liv said that the train was cancelled.

no.value: Amir forklarte at kundene allerede visste om forsinkelsen.

en.value: Amir explained that the clients already knew about the delay.

no.value: Sara fortalte at hun ikke rakk møtet.

en.value: Sara said that she didn’t make it to the meeting.

spans.value: Common reporting verbs include si, fortelle, forklare and svare. Their grammar is not identical.

no.value: Liv sa at hun jobbet hjemmefra.

en.value: Liv said that she was working from home.

no.value: Liv fortalte Jonas at hun jobbet hjemmefra.

en.value: Liv told Jonas that she was working from home.

spans.value: With si, the listener is commonly introduced with til.

no.value: Liv sa til Jonas at hun jobbet hjemmefra.

en.value: Liv said to Jonas that she was working from home.

spans.value: With fortelle, the listener can follow the verb directly.

no.value: Liv fortalte Jonas at hun jobbet hjemmefra.

en.value: Liv told Jonas that she was working from home.

spans.value: The content after at is a
subordinate clause (leddsetning)
. It uses
subordinate word order (leddsetningsordstilling)
. In particular, sentence adverbs such as ikke, aldri and allerede normally come before the finite verb.
Compare the direct statement and the report:
Original statement

no.value: Jeg jobber ikke på kontoret i dag.

en.value: I’m not working at the office today.

spans.value: Reported statement

no.value: Liv sa at hun ikke jobbet på kontoret den dagen.

en.value: Liv said that she was not working at the office that day.

spans.value: The key contrast is:

no.value: Hun jobbet ikke på kontoret.

en.value: She was not working at the office.

no.value: Han sa at hun ikke jobbet på kontoret.

en.value: He said that she was not working at the office.

spans.value: In the independent sentence, ikke follows the finite verb jobbet. In the subordinate clause after at, ikke comes before jobbet.
The same pattern applies to other sentence adverbs:

no.value: Amir hadde allerede ringt kundene.

en.value: Amir had already called the clients.

no.value: Jonas sa at Amir allerede hadde ringt kundene.

en.value: Jonas said that Amir had already called the clients.

no.value: Liv kommer kanskje senere.

en.value: Liv may come later.

no.value: Sara sa at Liv kanskje kom senere.

en.value: Sara said that Liv might come later.

spans.value: For the neutral reported-statement pattern taught here, use subordinate word order after at:

no.value: Jonas sa at Liv ikke jobbet hjemme.

en.value: Jonas said that Liv was not working at home.

spans.value: A compact rule for this lesson’s at-report patterns is: place ikke and similar sentence adverbs before the finite verb.
A yes-or-no question has no question word such as hva, hvor or når. In indirect speech, it normally begins with
om
, meaning whether or if.
Original question

no.value: Kan vi flytte presentasjonen?

en.value: Can we move the presentation?

spans.value: Reported question

no.value: Liv spurte om vi kunne flytte presentasjonen.

en.value: Liv asked whether we could move the presentation.

spans.value: The original question uses verb–subject order:

no.value: Kommer Liv tilbake i dag?

en.value: Is Liv coming back today?

spans.value: The reported question is a subordinate clause. It therefore uses subject–verb order:

no.value: Amir spurte om Liv kom tilbake den dagen.

en.value: Amir asked whether Liv was coming back that day.

spans.value: Compare the structures:

no.value: Har Amir ringt kundene?

en.value: Has Amir called the clients?

no.value: Sara spurte om Amir hadde ringt kundene.

en.value: Sara asked whether Amir had called the clients.

no.value: Jobber ikke Liv hjemme i dag?

en.value: Isn’t Liv working from home today?

no.value: Sara spurte om Liv ikke jobbet hjemme den dagen.

en.value: Sara asked whether Liv was not working from home that day.

spans.value: The report is not written as a direct question. It has no question mark when the whole sentence is a statement, and it does not retain question inversion.
Incorrect:

no.value: Sara spurte om hadde Amir ringt kundene.

en.value: 'Incorrect: Sara asked whether had Amir called the clients.'

spans.value: Natural Bokmål:

no.value: Sara spurte om Amir hadde ringt kundene.

en.value: Sara asked whether Amir had called the clients.

spans.value: The compact rule is: use om for a reported yes-or-no question, then use subordinate word order.

sections.title: Reporting questions with a question word

spans.value: When the original question already contains a question word, keep that word. In the basic indirect-question pattern, do not add om before it. If the question word is not the subject, the reported question uses ordinary subordinate word order.
Original question

no.value: Når kommer Liv tilbake?

en.value: When is Liv coming back?

spans.value: Reported question

no.value: Amir spurte når Liv kom tilbake.

en.value: Amir asked when Liv was coming back.

spans.value: Here, Liv is the subject and når refers to time. The original question uses inversion, but the reported question uses subject–verb subordinate order.

no.value: Hvor jobber Liv i dag?

en.value: Where is Liv working today?

no.value: Sara spurte hvor Liv jobbet den dagen.

en.value: Sara asked where Liv was working that day.

spans.value: When hvem or hva is itself the subject of the reported question, add som after the question word.

no.value: Hvem kommer tilbake i morgen?

en.value: Who is coming back tomorrow?

no.value: Sara spurte hvem som kom tilbake dagen etter.

en.value: Sara asked who was coming back the following day.

no.value: Hva skjedde på møtet?

en.value: What happened at the meeting?

no.value: Liv spurte hva som skjedde på møtet.

en.value: Liv asked what happened at the meeting.

spans.value: Do not add som when another word is the subject.

no.value: Hva kjøpte Liv?

en.value: What did Liv buy?

no.value: Sara spurte hva Liv kjøpte.

en.value: Sara asked what Liv bought.

no.value: Hvorfor har toget blitt innstilt?

en.value: Why has the train been cancelled?

no.value: Jonas spurte hvorfor toget hadde blitt innstilt.

en.value: Jonas asked why the train had been cancelled.

spans.value: With ikke, subordinate order remains visible:

no.value: Hvorfor kommer hun ikke til kontoret?

en.value: Why isn’t she coming to the office?

no.value: Sara spurte hvorfor hun ikke kom til kontoret.

en.value: Sara asked why she wasn’t coming to the office.

spans.value: A common mistake is to keep the original inversion.
Incorrect:

no.value: Amir spurte når kom Liv tilbake.

en.value: 'Incorrect: Amir asked when did Liv come back.'

spans.value: Natural Bokmål:

no.value: Amir spurte når Liv kom tilbake.

en.value: Amir asked when Liv was coming back.

spans.value: Om before a question word can instead be read as the preposition selected by spørre, but that reading is less direct and outside the basic indirect-question pattern taught here:

no.value: Sara spurte om hvorfor Liv jobbet hjemme.

en.value: Sara asked about why Liv was working from home.

spans.value: Preferred basic indirect-question form:

no.value: Sara spurte hvorfor Liv jobbet hjemme.

en.value: Sara asked why Liv was working from home.

spans.value: As an indirect-question marker in this lesson’s target pattern, use om only when the original question has no question word.
Commands and requests are often reported with be noen om å followed by an infinitive. The person after be is the person expected to perform the action.
Original request from Liv to Jonas

no.value: Send kundene en melding.

en.value: Send the clients a message.

spans.value: Jonas’s report

no.value: Liv ba meg om å sende kundene en melding.

en.value: Liv asked me to send the clients a message.

spans.value: The original message addresses Jonas as du, but Jonas reports his own role with meg.

no.value: Vent på meg utenfor stasjonen.

en.value: Wait for me outside the station.

no.value: Liv ba Jonas om å vente på henne utenfor stasjonen.

en.value: Liv asked Jonas to wait for her outside the station.

spans.value: For a negative command in the be noen om å construction, this lesson uses the pattern om ikke å + infinitive:

no.value: Ikke ring kundene ennå.

en.value: Don’t call the clients yet.

no.value: Amir ba meg om ikke å ringe kundene ennå.

en.value: Amir asked me not to call the clients yet.

spans.value: A stronger instruction can also be reported with si at someone must or should do something.

no.value: Du må sende meldingen før lunsj.

en.value: You must send the message before lunch.

no.value: Liv sa at jeg måtte sende meldingen før lunsj.

en.value: Liv said that I had to send the message before lunch.

spans.value: These patterns present the same instruction from slightly different angles:

no.value: Liv ba meg om å sende meldingen.

en.value: Liv asked me to send the message.

no.value: Liv sa at jeg måtte sende meldingen.

en.value: Liv said that I had to send the message.

spans.value: The first reports the request through be om å. The second reports the obligation as a statement with måtte.
Do not normally report a command by placing its imperative form after at.
Incorrect:

no.value: Liv sa at send kundene en melding.

en.value: 'Incorrect: Liv said that send the clients a message.'

spans.value: Natural alternatives:

no.value: Liv ba meg om å sende kundene en melding.

en.value: Liv asked me to send the clients a message.

no.value: Liv sa at jeg måtte sende kundene en melding.

en.value: Liv said that I had to send the clients a message.

spans.value: Norwegian does not require an automatic tense change in every report. The tense depends on the reporting time, whether the situation is still current, and how the speaker views it.
If the reporting verb is present and the information is still current, the original present tense often remains present.

no.value: Liv sier at hun er på toget.

en.value: Liv says that she is on the train.

no.value: Jonas sier at presentasjonen begynner klokka ett.

en.value: Jonas says that the presentation starts at one.

spans.value: A past reporting verb often creates a past viewpoint.

no.value: Liv sa at hun var på toget.

en.value: Liv said that she was on the train.

no.value: Jonas sa at presentasjonen begynte klokka ett.

en.value: Jonas said that the presentation started at one.

spans.value: However, present tense can remain when the reported information is still valid or is presented as a general fact.

no.value: Amir sa at kontoret stenger klokka fem.

en.value: Amir said that the office closes at five.

no.value: Læreren forklarte at norsk har to offisielle skriftformer.

en.value: The teacher explained that Norwegian has two official written forms.

spans.value: The report does not mechanically turn every present tense into past tense. Compare:

no.value: Liv sa at hun var syk.

en.value: Liv said that she was ill.

spans.value: This presents her illness from the earlier time.

no.value: Liv sa at hun er syk.

en.value: Liv said that she is ill.

spans.value: This is possible when the speaker presents her illness as still true now.
An event completed before another past reporting point commonly uses the
past perfect (pluskvamperfektum)
: hadde plus the past participle.
Original words from Amir

no.value: Jeg har allerede snakket med kundene.

en.value: I have already spoken to the clients.

spans.value: Jonas’s later report

no.value: Amir sa at han allerede hadde snakket med kundene.

en.value: Amir said that he had already spoken to the clients.

spans.value: The conversation with the clients happened before Amir’s statement, and both are viewed from the past.
A future action viewed from a past reporting point often uses skulle.
Original plan

no.value: Jeg skal komme tilbake i morgen.

en.value: I’m going to come back tomorrow.

spans.value: Later report

no.value: Liv sa at hun skulle komme tilbake dagen etter.

en.value: Liv said that she was going to come back the following day.

spans.value: Use tense to preserve the time relationship, not to perform a blind word-for-word conversion.
Indirect speech is told from the reporter’s point of view. Pronouns and references to time or place may therefore change.
Consider Liv speaking to Jonas. Liv is working from her home in Grünerløkka, while Jonas later reports from the office in Majorstuen, so the two speakers are in different places:

no.value: Jeg sender deg filen herfra i morgen.

en.value: I’ll send you the file from here tomorrow.

spans.value: Jonas reports this to Sara two days later from the office:

no.value: Liv sa at hun skulle sende meg filen derfra dagen etter.

en.value: Liv said that she would send me the file from there the following day.

spans.value: Several references have shifted:

items.value: jeg becomes hun because Jonas is speaking about Liv.
deg becomes meg because Jonas was the original listener.
herfra becomes derfra because Jonas is now somewhere else.
i morgen becomes dagen etter because the original tomorrow is now in the past.

spans.value: Useful time shifts include:

no.value: Hun sa at hun ikke kunne komme den dagen.

en.value: She said that she could not come that day.

no.value: Han forklarte at han hadde ringt dagen før.

en.value: He explained that he had called the day before.

no.value: De sa at de skulle reise dagen etter.

en.value: They said that they were going to leave the following day.

no.value: Liv sa at hun måtte dra da.

en.value: Liv said that she had to leave then.

spans.value: Useful place shifts include:

no.value: Hun sa at hun ventet der.

en.value: She said that she was waiting there.

no.value: Jonas fortalte at Liv skulle komme tilbake dit senere.

en.value: Jonas said that Liv was going to return there later.

spans.value: These changes are not compulsory when the reporter still shares the original time or place. Jonas may report Liv’s morning message later on the same day:

no.value: Liv sa at hun kommer hit i dag.

en.value: Liv said that she is coming here today.

spans.value: Here, i dag still means the same day, and hit still points to the office where Jonas is speaking.
The important question is not “Which words always change?” but “Do these words still point to the same person, day, and place from the reporter’s position?”
A common mistake is to preserve a pronoun even though its speaker has changed.
Original words from Liv:

no.value: Jeg ringer deg senere.

en.value: I’ll call you later.

spans.value: Jonas reporting to Sara:
Incorrect:

no.value: Liv sa at jeg skulle ringe deg senere.

en.value: 'Not: Liv said that I would call you later. (for the intended reported perspective)'

spans.value: Natural report:

no.value: Liv sa at hun skulle ringe meg senere.

en.value: Liv said that she would call me later.

spans.value: The incorrect version makes Jonas, rather than Liv, the person who will call.
Later, Sara phones Liv. She now has to pass on what Jonas told her.
Liv
Fikk du vite hva Jonas sa om meg?

blocks.translation: Did you find out what Jonas said about me?

spans.value: Sara
Ja. Jonas sa at toget ditt var innstilt, og at du jobbet hjemmefra.

blocks.translation: Yes. Jonas said that your train was cancelled and that you were working from home.

spans.value: Sara
Han fortalte også at du hadde bedt ham om å sende kundene en melding.

blocks.translation: He also said that you had asked him to send the clients a message.

spans.value: Liv
Sa han at Amir allerede hadde snakket med dem?

blocks.translation: Did he say that Amir had already spoken to them?

spans.value: Sara
Ja, han sa at Amir allerede hadde gjort det.

blocks.translation: Yes, he said that Amir had already done so.

spans.value: Liv
Flott. Spurte Amir når jeg kom tilbake?

blocks.translation: Great. Did Amir ask when I was coming back?

spans.value: Sara
Ja. Jonas sa at Amir hadde spurt når du kom tilbake til kontoret.

blocks.translation: Yes. Jonas said that Amir had asked when you were coming back to the office.

spans.value: The same information has now passed through more than one person. Pronouns change again because Sara is speaking directly to Liv: Jonas’s hun becomes Sara’s du. The time relationships also become more layered: Amir asked first, Jonas reported his question later, and Sara is now reporting Jonas’s account.
Even in a longer chain, the core decisions remain the same:

items.value: Use at to report a statement.
Use om for a yes-or-no question.
Keep the question word in an information question; use hvem or hva + som when the question word is the clause subject.
Use subordinate word order inside the report.
Report commands and requests with a structure such as be noen om å.
Choose tense, pronouns, and time or place expressions from the current reporting viewpoint.

sections.title: Transfer: a delivery at the wrong address

spans.value: Now move to a new everyday situation. Nora receives a message from a delivery driver while her neighbour Emil is away. The driver gives information, asks questions, and leaves an instruction. Later, Nora must tell Emil what happened.
The learner should report:

items.value: what the driver said about the parcel;
whether the driver asked a yes-or-no question;
what the driver wanted to know;
what the driver asked Nora or Emil to do;
when and where the events were supposed to happen from Nora’s later viewpoint.

spans.value: Without looking back, explain when a report uses at, when it uses om, what happens after a non-subject question word, and when subject hvem or hva requires som. Then report one statement, one question, and one command from a recent imaginary conversation, changing pronouns and time or place expressions wherever the new viewpoint requires it.

prompt.value: Classify each report by its complete message map. In this office dialogue, Jonas reports Liv's messages as hun and Amir's as han; in the report with meg, meg refers to Jonas. Choose the bucket that identifies original speaker, message function, and recipient only when recipient is stated. Do not infer a recipient.

explanation.value: Indirect speech shifts viewpoint and uses subordinate order: «at/om/question word + subject + sentence adverb + finite verb». Reported requests use «be + person + om å + infinitive».

items.text: Hun sa at toget til Bergen var innstilt.
Hun spurte om vi kunne flytte presentasjonen.
Hun ba meg også om å sende kundene en melding i dag.
Han sa at han allerede hadde snakket med dem.
Han spurte også når Liv kom tilbake til kontoret.
Hun sa at hun skulle komme tilbake hit i dag.

prompt.value: Build Jonas's report of Liv's update: Liv said, «Jeg jobber ikke hjemme.» Put the sentence adverb before the finite verb after at.
Build the indirect report of the direct question «Har Amir ringt kundene?» Use om and subject–verb subordinate order. The report is a statement, not a direct question.

Build one complete report containing both patterns. Report «Når kommer Liv tilbake?» and «Hva skjedde på møtet?» in one coordinated sentence. Keep the question words, use som after subject-question hva, and use neither om nor direct-question inversion.

Build one sentence reporting both instructions. Liv asked Jonas to wait for her outside the station, and Amir asked me not to call the clients yet. Use be + person + om å + infinitive, keeping the negative pattern natural.

Choose the complete set of reports that preserves all three time relationships: the office closing time is still a general fact, Liv's illness belonged only to the earlier day, and the client conversation happened before an earlier past report.

options.text: 1. Amir sa at kontoret stengte klokka fem. 2. Liv sa at hun var syk. 3. Amir sa at han allerede snakket med kundene.
options.why: This backshifts the continuing general fact and does not use past perfect for the event completed before the past report.

options.text: 1. Amir sa at kontoret stenger klokka fem. 2. Liv sa at hun var syk. 3. Amir sa at han allerede hadde snakket med kundene.
options.why: The present keeps the general fact current, the past presents the earlier illness, and the past perfect places the client conversation before the past report.

options.text: 1. Amir sa at kontoret stenger klokka fem. 2. Liv sa at hun er syk. 3. Amir sa at han allerede har snakket med kundene.
options.why: The present forms incorrectly present the earlier illness and completed past event as current from the required past viewpoint.

stem.value: Choose the set that matches all three contexts and uses meaningful tense rather than automatic backshifting.

prompt.value: Build Jonas's later report of Liv's message. Two days later, Jonas is in the office and reports to Sara. Liv originally said «Jeg sender deg filen herfra i morgen.» Apply the taught pronoun, tense, time, and place shifts.

Write 3 connected sentences in Norwegian. Sara is speaking directly to Liv now. Relay these three parts of Jonas's account as indirect speech, not direct quotes: Jonas said that Liv's train was cancelled and that she was working from home; he said that Liv had asked him to send the clients a message; and he said that Amir had asked when Liv was coming back to the office. Use at for statement reports, keep når in the reported information question, and use subordinate word order. Because Sara speaks to Liv, use du for Liv and ham for Jonas where needed.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept equivalent natural Bokmål variants only when they preserve all three messages and the requested viewpoint.

criteria.instruction: Relays all three specified parts as complete indirect reports rather than direct quotations.
Uses at for statement reports and keeps når in the reported information question.
Uses subordinate word order inside the reported at- and når-clauses.
Uses du for Liv and ham for Jonas where the new speaker perspective requires those forms.

prompt.value: Build Nora's indirect report of the driver's factual message: «Pakken er ikke på riktig adresse, og den er allerede levert.» Start with Nora fortalte and place ikke and allerede before their finite verbs after at.

Build one complete indirect report. The driver asked Nora «Er pakken på riktig adresse?», «Hvem leverte den?» and «Hvor bodde Emil?» Start with Nora fortalte. Use om only for the yes-or-no question, use hvem som for the subject question, and keep subordinate order without om for the hvor-question.
Build the report of the driver's instruction to Nora: «Legg pakken ved døren.» Start with Sjåføren ba Nora and use the be + person + om å + infinitive structure.

Build Nora's report to Emil the following evening from another place. Earlier, the driver told Nora «Jeg skal legge pakken her i morgen.» The planned action is today when Nora reports it. Change the driver's jeg, the original her, and i morgen consistently with the new viewpoint. Start with Nora sa til Emil.

Write a compact connected set of 5 Norwegian indirect reports in a new situation; do not copy a complete chapter example. You are Mina, speaking to Erik the next morning about yesterday's museum visit. A woman guide said «Utstillingen åpner klokka ti.», asked «Har Erik bestilt billett?», asked «Hvorfor kom dere sent?» and asked «Hvem tok med billettene?». She also told Mina «Vent utenfor.». Report all five messages indirectly. Use at for the statement, om only for the yes-or-no question, preserve question-word reports with subordinate order and som when the question word is the subject, and report the instruction with be noen om å. Keep the yesterday timeline and Mina's perspective when choosing pronouns and tense.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept equivalent natural Bokmål variants only when they preserve the specified message types, timeline, and speaker perspective.

criteria.instruction: Communicates the guide's statement, two information questions, yes-or-no question, and instruction as indirect reports.
Uses at for the statement, om only for the yes-or-no question, and question-word clauses without direct-question inversion.
Uses hvem som for the question in which hvem is the clause subject.
Reports the instruction with a natural be + person + om å + infinitive construction.
Uses a coherent past viewpoint and identifies Mina, Erik, and the guide consistently from Mina's position.
